{"id": "dcf366a0-8aa0-4d16-a681-d911a4c86fe5", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_vboJr9XWLMCnFkF1qmRbyL", "content": "[{'text': '## Documentation search results\\n\\n{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Introducing The CIS Amazon EKS Benchmark | Containers\",\"context\":\"## Containers\\\\n\\\\n# Introducing The CIS Amazon EKS Benchmark\\\\n\\\\nToday, we\u2019re announcing a new Center for Internet Security (CIS) benchmark for Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS). This new benchmark is optimized to help you accurately assess the security configuration of Amazon EKS clusters, including security assessments for nodes to help meet security and compliance requirements.\\\\n\\\\nSecurity is a critical consideration when configuring and maintaining Kubernetes clusters and applications. Amazon EKS provides secure, managed Kubernetes clusters by default, but you still need to ensure that you configure the nodes and applications securely and meet your security and compliance requirements. The CIS Kubernetes Benchmark provides good practice guidance on security configurations for unmanaged Kubernetes clusters where you typically manage the Kubernetes cluster control plane and nodes. The benchmark does not sufficiently cover the different configuration mechanisms used by Amazon EKS. This means that if you\u2019re using the CIS Kubernetes benchmark with EKS clusters you\u2019re faced with false positive errors. These errors incorrectly assert your clusters are not secure or properly configured. With the CIS Amazon EKS Benchmark, you now have guidance aligned to the Amazon EKS cluster configuration and you should use this benchmark to assess and configure security for your cluster nodes. You may use the recently published Amazon EKS Best Practices Guide for Security in conjunction with the CIS Amazon EKS Benchmark that we announce today.\\\\n\\\\nThe latest version of CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v1.5.1 provides guidance on security configurations for Kubernetes versions v1.15 for unmanaged Kubernetes clusters. The CIS Kubernetes Benchmark is scoped for implementations managing both the control plane, which includes `etcd`, API server, controller and scheduler, and the data plane, which is made up of one or more nodes. As Amazon EKS provides a fully managed control plane, not all of the recommendations from the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark are applicable as you are not responsible for configuring or managing the control plane. To ensure this scope is reflected with implementation specifics of Amazon EKS, we created the CIS Amazon EKS Benchmark starting from the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark and with the input of the community around specific configuration considerations for EKS clusters\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/containers/introducing-cis-amazon-eks-benchmark/\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Domain 3: Data access and integration\",\"context\":\"## AWS DevOps Agent: Managed topology\\\\n\\\\nAWS DevOps Agent handles topology differently from custom-built agents. AWS DevOps Agent automatically discovers and maps the resources and relationships within your applications. It builds topology graphs through several automated processes:\\\\n\\\\n- Scans your AWS accounts to identify compute, storage, networking, and database resources.\\\\n\\\\n- Analyzes AWS CloudFormation stacks, resource tags, and configuration data to find resource relationships.\\\\n\\\\n- Links infrastructure to deployment processes when connected to CI/CD pipelines.\\\\n\\\\n- Uses observability data from CloudWatch Application Signals and third-party tools, such as Dynatrace, to identify behavioral relationships.\\\\n\\\\nThe topology is interactive and queryable through the Operator Web App, with system-, container-, and resource-level views. During investigations, AWS DevOps Agent uses this topology to understand the blast radius, trace impact paths through dependency chains, and pinpoint root causes in distributed systems. It also identifies where resilience improvements have the most impact to make preventative recommendations. The AWS DevOps Agent doesn\u2019t only use topology resources. It can use additional data sources and AWS service APIs to investigate beyond the mapped boundary. Follow the **Credential management and access scoping** section to scope the agent\\'s IAM role\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/articles/ARSgVn7xNoSkiiRnqPi9A18w/domain-3-data-access-and-integration\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Faster Resolution with AWS DevOps Agent in the Support Center Console\",\"context\":\"### Security model\\\\n\\\\nAWS DevOps Agent operates with minimal permissions and maintains strict security boundaries throughout every interaction.\\\\n\\\\nAWS DevOps Agent takes the following security precautions:\\\\n\\\\n- **Read-only access only**\\\\nThe **DevOpsAgentRole-AgentSpace** IAM role uses the **AIDevOpsAgentAccessPolicymanaged** policy, providing strictly read-only access.\\\\n\\\\n- **Scoped and revocable credentials** \\\\nAWS DevOps Agent encrypts credentials, scopes the credentials to the specific Support interaction, and automatically revokes them when the investigation completes.\\\\n\\\\n- **Immutable audit trail** \\\\nAWS DevOps Agent records every action in an immutable journal. If you decline consent at any point, then AI-enhanced troubleshooting continues with standard AI-enhanced recommendations\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/articles/ARyeRSc6n6RySfv-_LihQD5w/faster-resolution-with-aws-devops-agent-in-the-support-center-console\"}]}}\\n\\n## Recent AWS announcements (What\\'s New)\\n\\nNewer than your training data may be.
